maria: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression on the canary after the kernel-selection tweak (merged earlier today). Host-side overhead (tokenize + parse) jumped on real traffic. attaching quick notes.

ajay: yikes. numbers?

maria: p95 latency for short chats +12%, CPU time on host up ~18% on serving nodes. KV cache hitrate dropped ~3% concurrently. flamegraph looks like parse/tokenize spikes.

ben: which change in kernel selector? the version affinity fallback?

maria: yes — the selector now prefers avx2-optimized kernels for certain sequence length buckets; runtime switches kernel at request start. I think switching cost is leaking into per-request path (micro-allocs + extra branch).

zoe: can you paste the perf snippet?

maria: ```
perf script | c++filt | flamegraph.pl > flame.svg
# top samples (host):
# 36% parse_request
# 18% tokenizer::tokenize_one
# 12% kernel_selector::choose
# 8% kv_cache::lookup
# 6% runtime::switch_kernel
```

ajay: that runtime::switch_kernel 6% is suspicious — should be async or cached.

maria: Agree. Also saw microbench: single-request path extra 120us on avg for short prompt (50 tokens). Batching gets worse because autobalancer reduces group size (preparse cost stalls batch formation).

casey: KV cache drop 3% could be explained if parse fragmentation changed keys. Any change to normalization/whitespace handling?

maria: No intentional change, but the selector adds metadata to hotpath which touches request proto earlier. Might affect canonicalization order.

ben: Repro locally? canary traces?

maria: Repro with load generator: `./bench --short-prompts --concurrency=200` shows the same delta. Pprof snapshot attached to thread (link: https://internal/pprof/9705551111).

zoe: Quick mitigation ideas: 1) revert kernel-selection to previous heuristic (safe), 2) memoize kernel decision per connection, 3) move switch_kernel off hot path (defer to worker thread). Thoughts?

ajay: 2+3 are low-risk. Memoize per-connection should cut repeated cost for multiplexed clients. But the immediate rollback might be fastest for canary.

maria: I pushed a small patch that memoizes kernel choice on connection object: cc @ajay @ben — PR #4982. Also added a metric `host_switch_kernel_count` to monitor.

infra-bot: deploy: canary rollout for PR #4982 started to eng-runtime-canary pool.

ben: good. Also suggest we add an experiment to measure KV key formation before/after to confirm cache key churn. I'll throw a quick instrument.

casey: For batching heuristics, maybe we should expose preparse budget metric so autoscaler knows to favor larger batches when parse cost spikes.

maria: noted. For short-term: rollback if canary doesn't improve within 30m. If memoize helps, promote and then follow up with kernel switch refactor.

ajay: I'll watch the canary metrics and alert if p95 stays > +6% after 10m.

maria: thanks. attaching short checklist: 
- reproduce locally (done)
- memoize per-connection (PR #4982)
- add host_switch_kernel_count metric (done)
- KV key instrumentation (ben)
- consider deferring heavy ops off hot path (follow-up)

zoe: ping me if we need a rollback. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy: canary PR #4982 rolled to 25% (10 hosts). Monitoring...

maria: logging improvement: `host_switch_kernel_count` increments dropped from ~5k/min to ~120/min on memoized canary hosts (early sign).

ben: nice. keep rolling if KV key churn stays stable.

maria: will update thread in 15m with final canary snapshot.

infra-bot: deploy: canary promoted to 75% (30 hosts).

maria: final: after promotion, p95 delta back to within baseline +/-1%. KV hitrate returned to normal. closing triage for now, follow-ups on kernel-switch refactor scheduled.

zoe: awesome, thanks team.
